questions.question: The UK tax year runs from…
questions.explanation: The tax year runs from 6 April to 5 April.

questions.question: The standard Personal Allowance (income you can earn tax-free) is…
questions.explanation: The standard Personal Allowance is £12,570. It's reduced for very high earners.

questions.question: How much savings interest can a basic-rate taxpayer earn tax-free (Personal Savings Allowance)?
questions.explanation: Basic-rate taxpayers get £1,000. Higher-rate taxpayers get £500.

questions.question: The Personal Savings Allowance for a higher-rate taxpayer is…
questions.explanation: Higher-rate taxpayers get £500. Additional-rate taxpayers get nothing.

questions.question: HMRC's trading allowance lets you earn how much a year in side income before you need to tell them?
questions.explanation: The trading allowance covers up to £1,000 of gross trading income.

questions.question: Selling your own old clothes online for less than you paid is usually…
options: Not trading, so normally no tax
questions.explanation: Selling personal belongings isn't trading. Buying items to resell for profit is.

questions.question: Online marketplaces now share seller details with HMRC once you sell around…
options: 30 items, or about £1,700, in a year
questions.explanation: Platforms report sellers who hit 30 sales or about £1,700 a year. Reporting isn't the same as owing tax.
questions.verify: Digital platform reporting thresholds on gov.uk

questions.question: The deadline for filing an online Self Assessment tax return is…
options: 31 January after the tax year ends
questions.explanation: Online returns are due by 31 January after the end of the tax year.

questions.question: The dividend allowance (2026/27) is…
questions.explanation: You can earn £500 of dividends tax-free outside an ISA.

questions.question: The Capital Gains Tax annual exempt amount is…
questions.explanation: You can make £3,000 of gains a year tax-free outside an ISA.
questions.verify: CGT annual exempt amount on gov.uk

questions.question: Marriage Allowance lets a lower earner transfer…
options: £1,260 of their Personal Allowance to a basic-rate partner
questions.explanation: Eligible couples can transfer £1,260, which saves up to £252 a year.

questions.question: Does Cash ISA interest use up your Personal Savings Allowance?
options: No: ISA interest is tax-free and separate
questions.explanation: ISA interest doesn't count towards your Personal Savings Allowance.

questions.question: Your tax code tells your employer…
options: How much tax-free pay you get
questions.explanation: The tax code reflects your allowances so the right tax is taken.

questions.question: National Insurance contributions build up your entitlement to…
questions.explanation: Your NI record decides your State Pension.

questions.question: You earn £800 from a small side hustle and have no other self-employed income. Under the trading allowance…
options: You normally don't need to tell HMRC
questions.explanation: Under £1,000 of gross trading income is usually covered by the trading allowance.

questions.question: The UK personal allowance means the first £12,570 of most people's income is:
options: Tax free (this threshold can change over time)
questions.explanation: The personal allowance is currently frozen at £12,570; thresholds can change.

questions.question: Most employees pay income tax through:
options: PAYE, deducted by the employer automatically
questions.explanation: PAYE handles most employees' tax automatically; check your tax code matches reality.

questions.question: Your tax code tells you:
options: How much tax-free pay you get before tax kicks in
questions.explanation: A wrong tax code means wrong deductions; check it against your actual situation.

questions.question: National Insurance contributions build entitlement to:
options: Certain benefits including the State Pension
questions.explanation: NI is separate from income tax and earns qualifying years toward benefits and the State Pension.

questions.question: The trading allowance lets you earn up to what from self-employment or casual income before declaring it:
questions.explanation: The £1,000 trading allowance covers casual income like small selling or odd jobs; above it you must register.

questions.question: If your side income exceeds £1,000 in a tax year, you should:
options: Register with HMRC and declare it, even if little or no tax is due
questions.explanation: Above the allowance, registration and declaration are required; that doesn't always mean tax is owed.

questions.question: Marriage Allowance lets a lower earner transfer 10% of their personal allowance to a partner, worth roughly:
questions.explanation: Marriage Allowance is worth up to about £252 a year in reduced tax (figure can change with allowances).

questions.question: Marriage Allowance eligibility requires the higher earner to be:
options: A basic-rate taxpayer, with the transferor earning under the personal allowance
questions.explanation: It works when one partner earns under £12,570 and the other is a basic-rate taxpayer.

questions.question: Dividend income above your dividend allowance is taxed:
options: At dividend tax rates depending on your band
questions.explanation: Dividends have their own allowance and rates; within ISAs they're tax-free.

questions.question: Child Benefit starts to be reduced when one parent's income exceeds roughly:
options: £50,000-£60,000, via the High Income Child Benefit Charge
questions.explanation: The charge claws back Child Benefit gradually from around £50k-£60k; thresholds change.

questions.question: VAT in the UK is generally:
questions.explanation: Standard-rate VAT is 20%, with reduced rates for some items.

questions.question: If you sell an item you've owned for years at a profit on a marketplace:
options: Personal possessions sales are often outside tax, but regular buying-to-sell counts as trading, so know the difference
questions.explanation: Clearing out your own things is usually fine; systematic reselling is a business with tax duties.

questions.question: Self-assessment tax returns for a tax year are normally due:
options: Online by 31 January the following year
questions.explanation: Miss 31 January and penalties start immediately, even if no tax is owed.

questions.question: The penalty for a late self-assessment return starts at:
options: An immediate £100 fine, growing with further delay
questions.explanation: The £100 penalty applies even if you owe no tax, so file on time regardless.

questions.question: Emergency tax can hit you when:
options: You start a new job or cash in a pension without the right tax code
questions.explanation: Emergency tax is usually corrected automatically once the right code applies, but worth checking.

questions.question: Salary sacrifice into a pension:
options: Reduces gross salary, cutting both tax and NI while boosting your pension
questions.explanation: Sacrifice saves NI as well as tax; check your employer's scheme before assuming.

questions.question: Tips you receive at work are:
options: Taxable income; how they're taxed depends on how they're distributed
questions.explanation: Tips are taxable whether cash or card; payroll handles card tips, cash tips you declare.

questions.question: Gains from selling investments or property above your annual capital gains allowance are:
options: Subject to capital gains tax at rates depending on your band
questions.explanation: CGT applies above the annual exempt amount (which has been cut recently, so check current figures).

questions.question: The rental income property allowance covers up to what for casual property income like lodgers or storage:
options: £7,500 via rent-a-room for furnished lodgings in your home
questions.explanation: £1,000 is the property allowance; rent-a-room relief is up to £7,500 for furnished lodgers in your own home.

questions.question: National Insurance voluntary contributions can be worth paying when:
options: You have gaps in your record that would reduce your State Pension
questions.explanation: Filling qualifying-year gaps can add meaningful State Pension for a small voluntary payment.

questions.question: Your P60 shows:
options: Your total pay and deductions for the tax year, from your employer
questions.explanation: Keep P60s; they're proof of income and tax paid for the year.

questions.question: A P45 is issued when:
options: You leave a job; it stops you being emergency-taxed at the next one
questions.explanation: Pass the P45 to a new employer or keep it if not working.

questions.question: Working from home may let you claim:
options: Limited tax relief for extra household costs, via your employer or tax return
questions.explanation: The relief is for extra costs of working from home, not general living costs; claims are modest.

questions.question: Gifting money and inheritance tax: gifts made within 7 years of death can:
options: Count toward the estate if you die within 7 years, tapering with time
questions.explanation: Large gifts aren't immediately tax-free; the 7-year clock matters for estates above thresholds.

questions.question: If HMRC sends you a tax calculation (P800) showing you've overpaid tax:
options: Check it and claim your refund; you're entitled to your own money
questions.explanation: P800s can show refunds owed or underpayments; verify before acting either way.
